subject: Slice-to-Commit conversion: invoice routing and VAT evidence
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@edgescale.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@edgescale.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question on Oct slice->commit conversion & invoice lines

Hi Ava,

We spotted a conversion on Oct 12 where 40 transient "slice" seats were converted to 10 committed seats mid-period. The invoice that followed (Invoice #7687) shows both a prorated charge and a separate adjustment line that looks like a one-time uplift. Can you confirm:

- How the prorate was calculated (days in period vs. effective date).
- Whether the adjustment is a credit or a charge tied to plan change fees.
- What evidence you can provide for VAT treatment — our finance team needs a line-by-line proof for cross-border VAT reclaim.

Attaching the invoice (pdf) and our internal calc of what we expected. Can we get a short breakdown so we can clear this with our AP?

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Finance, EdgeScale Inc

Attachment: edgescale_invoice_7687.pdf (invoice, 1 page)
Attachment: client_calc_rough.xlsx (their calc, 1 sheet)

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@edgescale.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct slice->commit conversion & invoice lines

Hi Marta — thanks for the note and the attachments. Short answers up-front, full breakdown below:

- Prorate basis: calendar days in billing period; conversion effective 2026-10-12 so line items split pro-rata by days.
- Adjustment line: one-time conversion fee that was mis-labeled; it should have been shown as a negative credit and has been reprocessed in our billing system.
- VAT evidence: we can provide a CSV export of invoice line items + the pro-rata calc and a confirmation letter for tax teams.

I'm looping in Jonas and Kimberly to confirm the credit path and to push a corrected invoice (and the CSV) to you by Friday. If you need the corrected invoice sooner for AP, let me know and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pro_rata_calc_edgescale.xlsx (new calc, 1 sheet)

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Question on Oct slice->commit conversion & invoice lines

Jonas / Kim — forwarding EdgeScale's ask. Key points:

1) They converted 40 transient slices -> 10 committed on 2026-10-12. Billing shows: prorated charge for remaining days + an "adjustment" line of $1,200 that looks like a plan-change fee. EdgeScale expects either a credit or clearer labeling.
2) They need VAT line-item evidence for cross-border reclaim (they're EU entity invoiced through US entity).

Proposal: issue a corrected invoice that
  - replaces the ambiguous adjustment with a negative credit if we mischarged,
  - adds an exported CSV with invoice_line_id, sku, qty, unit_price, start_date, end_date, taxable_country, VAT_rate, VAT_amount, and the prorate denominator we used,
  - include a one-paragraph letter on company letterhead describing our prorate policy and the effective conversion date.

Can we OK a $0 net-change credit if the adjustment was erroneous? If it's a legitimate conversion fee per contract, we'll need to confirm the clause in the MA.

Also: collection impact — they flagged AP hold until cleared. If we issue corrected invoice and CSV, will that unblock payment? If so, we should expedite.

Thoughts?

- Ava

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Question on Oct slice->commit conversion & invoice lines

Thanks Ava — I pulled the billing journal for ES-0421 and confirmed: the $1,200 line was tagged as "conversion fee" in a historic template but should have been applied as a negative adjustment for this specific conversion (we never intended to charge them twice). Approve the following action items and I'll route to Ops for reissue:

Action items:
- Billing Ops: void Invoice #7687 and reissue Invoice #7687-R with corrected lines (prorate shown explicitly: 2026-10-12 -> 2026-10-31 days = 20/31).
- Finance: apply a $1,200 credit against the reissued invoice and mark original adjustment as reversed.
- Tax/Compliance: generate CSV export with per-line VAT attributes and a signed letter on Redwood letterhead confirming "no additional fee" was intended for this conversion.
- CS/AE (Ava): send the reissued invoice and CSV to EdgeScale and ask AP if a short note from Redwood will clear the hold.

Kimberly — can you confirm we can margin-neutral reverse the adjustment? If yes, I will instruct Billing Ops to expedite and flag invoice as "CORRECTED — PRIOR PAYMENT PENDING".

Jonas
VP, Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
